Finite coordinate sets I and J; filtered finite measure space (Omega,m,mu,F); horizon T; integrands eta_ij; drift coordinates b_i; path X; set K; scalar f; v=(b_i), sigma_j=(eta_ij.process).

I,J are finite types; I has decidable equality. T is any nonnegative real. X:[0,infinity)×Omega→R^I, b_i:[0,infinity)×Omega→R, f:R^I→R, K⊆R^I. Time measure lambda_T is Lebesgue measure on [0,T], represented on nonnegative reals.

Assumptions: mu is finite. Each eta_ij is strongly progressive with (omega,t)↦eta_ij(t,omega) in L²(mu⊗lambda_T). For every i, b_i(·,omega) is lambda_T-integrable for mu-a.e. omega. X(·,omega) is continuous on [0,T] mu-a.e. and, on a mu-full set, X(t,omega)∈K for every t≤T. At every w∈K, f is C² at w in the ambient Euclidean space. There is no compactness assumption on K, no Brownian motion assumption, and no progressivity assumption on b or X.

Conclusion: For mu-a.e. omega, both t↦Df(X(t,omega))[v(t,omega)] and t↦(1/2)∑_{j∈J}D²f(X(t,omega))[sigma_j(t,omega),sigma_j(t,omega)] are integrable against lambda_T.

Quantifier order: Universally quantify all listed data. For each i assume pathwise drift integrability mu-a.e.; assume path continuity and all-time range inclusion mu-a.e. Conclusion has one mu-a.e. omega quantifier covering both integrability assertions.

Scope: Pathwise absolute integrability on the fixed horizon [0,T]; not integrability over Omega of these time integrals. T may be zero. No stochastic equation linking X, b and eta is assumed.

Constant dependencies: No existential numerical constants or rates.
